sentiment.rationale: The company delivered strong Q4 results with room nights, gross bookings, and revenue all exceeding the high end of prior guidance, and management raised its full-year 2026 outlook to grow approximately 100 basis points ahead of its long-term growth algorithm while expanding margins. However, a significant portion of the reported growth is attributed to favorable FX (approximately 500 basis points in Q4 and 200-300 basis points for the full year), and management's forward guidance is a target rather than a formal raised guidance range, tempering the score. The organic constant-currency growth still exceeds the long-term algorithm, and management expresses confident language about reinvestment and AI opportunities, supporting a moderately positive score.

summary.revenue: Q4 2025 revenue was $6.3 billion, up 16% year-over-year (approximately 11% on a constant currency basis). Full year 2025 revenue was $26.9 billion, up 13% year-over-year (approximately 10% on a constant currency basis).
summary.eps: Q4 2025 GAAP EPS was $44.22, up 38% year-over-year. Adjusted EPS was $48.80, up 17% year-over-year. Full year 2025 GAAP EPS was $165.57, down 4% year-over-year. Adjusted EPS was $228.06, up 22% year-over-year.
summary.guidance: For Q1 2026, the company expects room night growth of 5%-7%, gross bookings growth of 14%-16%, revenue growth of 14%-16%, and Adjusted EBITDA growth of 10%-14%. For FY 2026, the company targets constant currency top-line growth approximately 100 basis points ahead of its long-term growth algorithm, with gross bookings and revenue up low-double-digits, Adjusted EBITDA growing faster than revenue, and Adjusted EPS up mid-teens.
summary.margin: Q4 2025 net income margin was 22.5% (19.5% in Q4 2024). Adjusted EBITDA margin was 34.6% (33.8% in Q4 2024). Full year 2025 net income margin was 20.1% (24.8% in 2024). Adjusted EBITDA margin was 36.9% (35.0% in 2024).
key_risks: Adverse FX changes impacting adjusted fixed operating expenses
An indirect tax matter accrual of $44 million
Potential impact of geopolitical and macroeconomic environment on consumer spending and travel patterns
Rapid technological changes and competition, including from large language models
Slightly lower ADRs and shorter length of stay in the US, indicating some consumer segments are being thoughtful on discretionary spending
key_opportunities: Advancing Generative AI capabilities to enhance traveler and partner value
Connected Trip strategy with transactions growing in the high-20% range
Growth in Asia and the US, with Asia delivering low double-digit room night growth
Flights business with 68 million airline tickets booked, up 37% year-over-year
Alternative accommodations with supply up approximately 8% to 8.6 million listings
Genius loyalty program with Level 2 and 3 travelers representing high 50% share of room nights
Transformation Program enabling approximately $550 million in annual run-rate savings
